Banks’ data breaches: India in constant state of digital pandemic; new vaccine needed regularly, say experts
sum: Since July, at least seven banks – including the largest lender State Bank of India -- have been victim to data breaches and cybersecurity attacks, causing critical customer data to be exposed to the Dark Web. The regulator, Reserve Bank of India, since October 19, has issued two advisories to lenders to tighten controls and set timelines for controls.

The deeper concern is that when banks give application programming interfaces (APIs) to non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) – by allowing their core systems to exchange data and allow for transactions linked to loan allocations or forex cards, the APIs are the portion which could be most compromised. Attackers – who rarely use the front door to break in – can hijack these trusted connections to carry out fund transfers or customer details from the bank.

In October 2026, while ICICI Bank's internal servers were not breached directly, cybercriminals compromised the APIs which linked ICICI Bank’s systems to NBFCs. Hackers manipulated these payment gateways to trigger over 700 unauthorised instant loan transfers, stealing approximately $2 million (approx. Rs 17 crore), media reports said.
“Historically, NBFCs, fintechs, have always been the weakest link and soft target,” says Yash Kadakia, founder of Security Brigade, a cyber security company.

Despite the heightened sense of caution, experts say banks, besides large corporates, remain in constant risk of future cyber-attacks. “We are in a constant state of digital pandemic. Whenever the new virus is coming, we have to take a vaccination for it,” says Ritesh Bhatia, founder of V4WEB Cybersecurity, who is a cybercrime investigator, incident response expert and data privacy consultant.

Just after announcing the September-ended quarterly earnings, SBI chairman C.S. Setty called the data breach at the bank – announced on October 21 -- in which some customers’ data was exposed on the dark web, “definitely an issue of concern”. SBI had received alerts from its threat intelligence service provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In on October 16 that its customers’ data was available on the dark web.

The Nifty Realty index declined 1.4%, with real estate stocks facing pressure amid concerns that a sustained rise in inflation could translate into higher bond yields and tighter liquidity.

State Bank of India stock: SBI trims December hike call to 25 bps
sum: State Bank of India's Economic Research Department has lowered its forecast for the Reserve Bank of India's December rate increase, pointing to easing pressure on the rupee and stronger foreign capital inflows. The change was reported by The Economic Times on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

SBI Research now expects a 25-basis-point increase at the December policy meeting, compared with its earlier 50-basis-point projection. The report said improved external conditions, renewed foreign fund inflows and reduced pressure on the Indian rupee had shifted the balance of probabilities.

The research unit put the chance of the December increase being the final hike in the current cycle at 50:50. It also said the terminal repo rate could reach 5.75 percent. The RBI raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent in October, its first increase in almost four years.

SBI Research expects Indian inflation to stay above 6 percent in November before easing. It cited early November price trends from the Department of Consumer Affairs and said expectations of three or four consecutive rate increases now appear to be an outlier.

The report also pointed to lower money-market pressure and foreign institutional inflows of 7.65 billion US dollars since November 6. For lenders, the revised path would imply a less aggressive near-term rate cycle, although elevated inflation and currency volatility remain important risks for funding costs and credit demand.

State Bank of India describes itself as India's largest commercial bank by assets, deposits, branches and employees. The bank operates through a broad commercial-banking platform and publishes financial results, ratings, Basel disclosures and shareholder information through its investor-relations operation.

SBI's scale gives it a broad exposure to Indian credit conditions, while the RBI's policy path remains a key macroeconomic factor for the banking sector. The company's investor-relations page is available at State Bank of India.

Banks, stock markets closed today? Check city-wise bank holidays and trading schedule for November
sum: Even when physical bank branches are closed, digital banking channels remain operational.

Both the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) are closed today, Tuesday, November 10, on account of Diwali-Balipratipada. Trading is suspended across equity, equity derivatives, debt markets, capital markets, electronic gold receipts, and securities lending segments. This break follows Sunday's special Muhurat Trading session and Monday's regular trading session. Normal trading across stock exchanges will resume on Wednesday, November 11.

Meanwhile, bank branches across India are not observing a uniform nationwide holiday today. Under the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regional calendar, bank branches in Ahmedabad, Belapur, Bengaluru, Dehradun, Gangtok, Mumbai, and Nagpur are shut for Diwali celebrations, including Laxmi Puja, Govardhan Puja, and Vikram Samvat New Year Day. In contrast, branches in cities such as Kanpur and Lucknow remain open today. Account holders of major lenders including State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and Axis Bank should verify local branch schedules before planning a visit.
Upcoming holiday schedule and essential banking services for November

The festive closures will shift to other regions on Wednesday, November 11. Bank branches in Gangtok, Imphal, Kanpur, Kolkata, Lucknow, and Shimla will close tomorrow for Laxmi Puja, Ningol Chakkouba, Bhai Dooj, and Chitragupt Jayanti. Later in the month, Shillong branches will observe a holiday on November 13 for the Wangala Festival. Standard weekend breaks follow on November 14 (second Saturday) and November 15 (Sunday).

Branches across Patna and Ranchi will shut on November 16 for Chhath Puja. Further regional closures include Dehradun on November 20 for Igas-Bagwal, Shillong on November 23 for Seng Kut Snem, and Bengaluru on November 27 for Kanakadasa Jayanthi. On November 24, bank branches across major centres, including New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Hyderabad, will close for Guru Nanak Jayanti. Remaining weekend breaks fall on November 22, 28 (fourth Saturday), and 29 .

SBI Card stock in focus after profit rises on lower credit costs
sum: SBI Cards and Payment Services reported a sharp rise in second-quarter profit on October 23, 2026, as improving asset quality reduced provisions. Reuters, published by The Hindu BusinessLine, reported that profit after tax reached INR 778 crore for the quarter ended September 30, compared with INR 445 crore a year earlier.

Loan-loss provisions fell 36.6 percent year over year to INR 819 crore. Gross non-performing assets stood at 1.90 percent at the end of September, down 14 basis points from three months earlier, after the company tightened credit underwriting to address delinquencies.

Total revenue from operations rose 3.6 percent year over year to INR 5,141 crore. Card spending increased 3 percent to INR 1.11 lakh crore, while cards-in-force grew 8 percent to 23.2 million. The figures point to continued volume growth, although the earnings improvement was driven more clearly by lower credit costs than by revenue expansion.

SBI Card's next focus is balancing expansion in card usage with underwriting discipline. Retail and corporate spending supported credit growth in the September quarter, while the lower provision burden gives profitability more room if asset quality remains stable.

SBI Cards and Payment Services issues credit cards in India and serves consumer and corporate spending needs. The company is a unit of State Bank of India and operates in the Indian payments and consumer-finance market. Its business combines card issuance, transaction spending and credit underwriting, making asset quality and funding costs central investment considerations.

Why SBI shares fell sharply after Q2
sum: State Bank of India faced a sharp stock pullback as soaring bond yields and rising operating expenses dragged core operating profits well below expectations, despite headline earnings getting a lift from one-off subsidiary stake sales. Discover how analysts view the true underlying valuation of its vast subsidiary network.

State Bank of India beat street estimates with both the topline and net profit. The net interest margin beat expectations, driven by strong credit growth and continued asset-quality improvement. Yet the stock fell sharply by 4.5% from the day's high to the day's low of ₹961.2, soon after the second-quarter earnings were released, before recovering slightly.
That's because the operating profit was well below estimates.

The country's largest bank booked a ₹7,288 crore pre-tax gain from selling a 6.3% stake in SBI Funds Management. The company also made ₹2,410 crore, net of taxes, from selling shares in the recently concluded National Stock Exchange (NSE) IPO. However, the profit has been credited to capital reserves, not the profit and loss statement.

We were expecting around ₹17,000 crore in other income during this quarter, but it has come at around ₹11,000 crore. So maybe certain treasury loss has come into the picture due to hardening of yields. SAMEER SAWANT, RESEARCH ANALYST, MIRAE ASSET SHAREKHAN

Regulations require all Indian banks to hold a portion of their reserves in government bonds. Compared money in government securities, making them vulnerable to sharp swings in yields. The recent increase in government bond yields requires them to mark down the value of their investments.

The sharp deviation between profit after tax and operating profit suggests underlying weakness. Cost pressures are visible. Operating expenses rose 9.6% year on year and 15.6% in the last three months. Cost-to-income ratio worsened to 49.82% by September 2026 from 46.71% at the end of June 2026.

sum: New Delhi: Geopolitical developments, especially growing concerns about renewed conflict between the US and Iran, crude oil prices, and quarterly earnings will be the major drivers for stock markets this week, analysts said.
In addition, US midterm elections, foreign investor trading activity, and macroeconomic data announcements will also be tracked by market investors.

“Markets will remain focused on the September quarter earnings season, key economic data releases and global developments this week. Investors will assess corporate performance for signs of sustained revenue growth, margin resilience and improving demand. Banking results will offer insights into credit growth, deposit mobilisation and asset quality, while automobile, consumer and industrial companies will provide a broader assessment of domestic demand conditions,” Ajit Mishra, SVP â€“ Research, Religare Broking, said.
Crude oil prices will remain an important variable, with elevated levels amid geopolitical uncertainty posing risks to imported inflation, the rupee and corporate margins, he said.
Movements in US Treasury yields, foreign institutional investor flows and currency markets will also influence near-term sentiment and the sustainability of the recent recovery, Mishra added.

“Key events to watch this week include the US midterm elections, US PMI and India’s HSBC PMI. On the earnings front, M&M, Bajaj Finserv, ITC, Dabur, Apollo Hospitals, BSE, Cummins India and Hindalco will be in focus,” Siddhartha Khemka – Head of Research, Wealth Management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd, said.

State Bank of India has announced its General Meeting scheduled for May 15, 2026, for the election of directors under Regulation 21 of SBI General Regulations, 1955. The meeting represents a significant corporate governance milestone for India's largest public sector bank.

The General Meeting will be conducted on Friday, May 15, 2026, at 03:00 PM at State Bank Auditorium, State Bank Bhavan, Madame Cama Road, Mumbai-400021. Shareholders holding shares in physical or dematerialized form as of the cut-off date February 13, 2026, are eligible to participate in the voting process. Once a vote is cast, shareholders cannot modify their choice subsequently.

The Notice of General Meeting was published in the Gazette of India on March 23, 2026, and in newspapers with wide circulation on March 24, 2026, as per Regulation 21 of SBI General Regulations. The broader market also mirrored the weakness, with the Nifty Midcap 100 falling 1.64 per cent and the Nifty Smallcap 100 declining 1.65 per cent.
Indian equity benchmarks continued to fall sharply in Thursday's trade as a fresh spike in crude oil prices amid renewed escalation in the West Asia conflict weighed on investor sentiment.
At the opening bell, the 30-share BSE Sensex pack tumbled 992.53 points to 75,871.18, while the NSE Nifty50 index dropped 310.55 points to 23,556.30.

The sharp selloff wiped out nearly Rs 5.6 lakh crore from the BSE's total market capitalisation (m-cap) during early trade. Investor wealth, as reflected by the BSE m-cap, declined by Rs 5.63 lakh crore to Rs 436.27 lakh crore, compared with Rs 441.90 lakh crore in the previous session.

VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, said, "External headwinds have pushed the market into a weak zone. With the war continuing to rage with no signs of let up and Brent crude again bouncing back to $100 levels, the weakness is likely to persist. Even though DIIs are continuously buying in the market, DII buying is not helping the market to recover since FIIs are sustained sellers and show no signs of reversing their strategy in this uncertain global environment."

He added, "For investors, markets can be very frustrating during certain times. This is one such time. The lesson from market history is that attitude and temperament are important in these trying times. Experiences from previous geopolitical conflicts tell us that markets bounce back smartly once the conflicts get over. Therefore, investors should remain invested and continue with systematic investment plans."

SBI chairman calls for level playing tax field for bank deposits, says equities don’t need tax favours any
sum: Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the bank's launch of a project to assess and finance new age infrastructure projects, Setty said that globally neither equity or bank deposits are given any special treatment.

"Globally also we have not seen anywhere where the bank deposits are given any special treatment, but at the same time equity instruments are also not given a special treatment in many jurisdictions.In an evolving equity environment, probably those benefits were justified. (But) now I think there should be a level playing field for the financial savings instruments," Setty said.

At present, returns on deposits attract taxation as per a taxpayer's tax slab which may go up to 30% while equity returns are taxed at 12.5% for long-term gains with a holding of more than a year above Rs 1.25 lakh. Equity investments sold within a year are taxed at a rate of 20% with a 0.1% Securities Transaction Tax (STT).

mutual funds on par with fixed deposits (FDs) doing away the tax arbitrage. Both debt investments and fixed deposits are now taxed as per the investor's marginal income tax slab, without any indexation benefit which was a major tax advantage for debt funds, allowing a 3-year period to adjust for inflation.
The Economic Survey released earlier this week also pointed towards the structural change in Indian household savings.
The share of deposits in financial savings having dropped to 35.2% in FY25 from 57.9% in FY12, though higher than the 31.95% reported in FY22.

"Equity investments, which were once ancillary to household balance sheets, have increasingly become a significant component of financial wealth, supported by broader participation and more diversified channels of access," the economic survey said.
